{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment within the existing Spring-based modular architecture, preserving current public APIs unless a user story requires an extension.",
    "Use Kafka topics as the persistence and changelog mechanism for repository state, with a local off-heap cache for stateful stream-processing access.",
    "Treat producer acknowledgements as the authoritative signal for safely flushing offsets and state, using coordinated success and failure handling.",
    "Implement intelligent flushing with retryable, idempotent operations and recovery behavior after process restart.",
    "Implement the CoAP source as an optional module with configurable endpoint, method, polling or subscription behavior, payload handling, and connection timeouts.",
    "Use the existing security and configuration abstractions for secured HDFS and Sqoop integration rather than introducing a separate credential-management system.",
    "Implement the Java receptor client as a REST client with configurable Diego endpoint, authentication, request timeouts, JSON serialization, and error handling.",
    "Implement ModuleRunner as a Spring Boot executable and make deployment properties available through standard Boot property binding and environment-variable overrides.",
    "Document deployment properties using representative properties-file examples and identify required, optional, default, and security-sensitive settings.",
    "Prefer backward-compatible configuration defaults and provide validation errors for unsupported or incomplete configurations."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The work is performed by one experienced Java/Spring developer familiar with Kafka, Hadoop, REST, and container deployment.",
    "An existing source repository, build system, test framework, CI pipeline, and module conventions are available and do not require migration.",
    "The required Kafka, HDFS, Diego, CoAP, and container test environments can be run locally or are available as shared test services.",
    "The specification does not define detailed APIs, wire formats, performance targets, or compatibility matrices; reasonable designs will be selected based on existing project conventions.",
    "The Kafka-backed repository may use an existing Kafka Streams or equivalent state-store abstraction, with implementation limited to integrating the repository and changelog behavior rather than developing a new storage engine.",
    "Offset and state flushing changes are limited to the stream-processing module and its producer acknowledgement path; no redesign of the complete messaging protocol is required.",
    "CoAP support covers the commonly required client-side source functionality and does not include a general-purpose CoAP server, full protocol proxying, or every optional CoAP extension.",
    "Secured HDFS support uses existing Hadoop security mechanisms such as Kerberos, delegation tokens, or configured Hadoop credentials; creation of an enterprise identity-management service is out of scope.",
    "The Java receptor client covers the REST APIs needed by the current XD use cases, not every Diego receptor endpoint.",
    "ModuleRunner completes remaining deployment-property work and container startup integration but does not replace all existing XD container deployment tooling.",
    "Documentation is maintained in the project's existing documentation format and publication process.",
    "Estimates include implementation, developer testing, code review preparation, and defect correction, but exclude project management, external release approval delays, and calendar waiting time."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and architecture planning",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing modules, configuration model, messaging flow, persistence abstractions, deployment model, and test conventions; refine the implementation design and identify integration points for all eight user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Development environment and test-fixture preparation",
      "activity_description": "Prepare or extend local test fixtures and mocks for Kafka, producer acknowledgements, CoAP, secured HDFS, Diego receptor REST calls, and Spring Boot container startup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka-changelog-backed Spring Data repository",
      "activity_description": "Implement the repository integration backed by Kafka changelog data, including off-heap local data affinity, serialization and deserialization, lifecycle behavior, recovery handling, configuration, unit tests, and focused integration tests for U1.",
      "most_likely_effort": 88
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Intelligent offset flushing",
      "activity_description": "Extend stream-processing acknowledgement flow so offsets are flushed only according to successful module-producer acknowledgements, with batching, failure handling, retries, restart behavior, configuration, and tests for U2.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Intelligent state flushing",
      "activity_description": "Coordinate repository or state-store flushes with successful producer acknowledgements, including ordering guarantees, failure and retry behavior, recovery semantics, configuration, and tests for U3.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "CoAP source module",
      "activity_description": "Develop the optional CoAP source module, including endpoint and request configuration, payload conversion, lifecycle management, timeout and retry behavior, error handling, module registration, documentation hooks, and unit/integration tests for U4.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Deployment properties documentation",
      "activity_description": "Document the properties-file deployment manifest, including property descriptions, defaults, required values, examples, environment overrides, and validation guidance for U5.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Secured HDFS support for Sqoop jobs",
      "activity_description": "Add or complete secured HDFS and Sqoop configuration, credential propagation, authentication setup, secure filesystem access, failure diagnostics, backward-compatible behavior, and tests for U6.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Java Diego receptor client",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Java REST client for required Diego receptor operations, including request and response models, authentication, connection configuration, timeouts, HTTP error mapping, logging, and client tests for U7.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Spring Boot ModuleRunner and deployment properties",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner for container-managed execution, complete remaining deployment-property binding and validation, support environment-based configuration, integrate module startup and shutdown, and add startup and container-oriented tests for U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 128
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature configuration and compatibility integration",
      "activity_description": "Integrate newly introduced configuration properties, defaults, validation, module discovery, dependency declarations, version compatibility, and interactions among repository, acknowledgement, source, client, and runner features.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end and failure-recovery testing",
      "activity_description": "Create and execute end-to-end scenarios covering acknowledged and failed messages, offset and state recovery, Kafka changelog restoration, CoAP ingestion, secure HDFS access, receptor calls, and Boot container startup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Regression testing and defect correction",
      "activity_description": "Run the existing unit, integration, and regression suites; diagnose compatibility issues; correct defects discovered across existing modules and the new increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A14",
      "activity_name": "Packaging, CI updates, and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Update build and packaging metadata, CI jobs, example configurations, release notes, migration notes, and final code-quality checks for the completed increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 832
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring-based modular architecture, preserving current public APIs unless a user story requires an extension.
Use Kafka topics as the persistence and changelog mechanism for repository state, with a local off-heap cache for stateful stream-processing access.
Treat producer acknowledgements as the authoritative signal for safely flushing offsets and state, using coordinated success and failure handling.
Implement intelligent flushing with retryable, idempotent operations and recovery behavior after process restart.
Implement the CoAP source as an optional module with configurable endpoint, method, polling or subscription behavior, payload handling, and connection timeouts.
Use the existing security and configuration abstractions for secured HDFS and Sqoop integration rather than introducing a separate credential-management system.
Implement the Java receptor client as a REST client with configurable Diego endpoint, authentication, request timeouts, JSON serialization, and error handling.
Implement ModuleRunner as a Spring Boot executable and make deployment properties available through standard Boot property binding and environment-variable overrides.
Document deployment properties using representative properties-file examples and identify required, optional, default, and security-sensitive settings.
Prefer backward-compatible configuration defaults and provide validation errors for unsupported or incomplete configurations.
assumptions: The work is performed by one experienced Java/Spring developer familiar with Kafka, Hadoop, REST, and container deployment.
An existing source repository, build system, test framework, CI pipeline, and module conventions are available and do not require migration.
The required Kafka, HDFS, Diego, CoAP, and container test environments can be run locally or are available as shared test services.
The specification does not define detailed APIs, wire formats, performance targets, or compatibility matrices; reasonable designs will be selected based on existing project conventions.

The Kafka-backed repository may use an existing Kafka Streams or equivalent state-store abstraction, with implementation limited to integrating the repository and changelog behavior rather than developing a new storage engine.
Offset and state flushing changes are limited to the stream-processing module and its producer acknowledgement path; no redesign of the complete messaging protocol is required.
CoAP support covers the commonly required client-side source functionality and does not include a general-purpose CoAP server, full protocol proxying, or every optional CoAP extension.

Secured HDFS support uses existing Hadoop security mechanisms such as Kerberos, delegation tokens, or configured Hadoop credentials; creation of an enterprise identity-management service is out of scope.
The Java receptor client covers the REST APIs needed by the current XD use cases, not every Diego receptor endpoint.
ModuleRunner completes remaining deployment-property work and container startup integration but does not replace all existing XD container deployment tooling.
Documentation is maintained in the project's existing documentation format and publication process.
Estimates include implementation, developer testing, code review preparation, and defect correction, but exclude project management, external release approval delays, and calendar waiting time.
